newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end up, then lose ground after AGAs.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end up, then lose ground after AGAs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures mostly ended higher Wednesday in a lackluster session, then lost ground on ACCESS when AGA reported a weekly stock build at the high end of expectations, industry sources said.

November climbed 4.1 cents to close at $2.096 per million British thermal units, then dipped to $2.071 on ACCESS. Dec traded at $2.28 in the after-hours session after earlier settling 3.6 cents higher at $2.298. Others also ended up. "I'm not sure why prices were so strong early today, but the AGA report brought prices down on ACCESS," said a Houston trader, adding cash could soften next month amid weak demand.
Most expected slower injections next month to put supply and demand out of balance unless some early heating loads kick in to pick up the slack.
Technically, traders still pegged November support in the $2.00 area, with resistance at $2.12 and then at the recent high of $2.305.

Cash sources said October Gulf Coast prices firmed slightly Wednesday to the low-to-mid $1.80s, with Oct gas at the Hub talked modestly higher at $1.86-1.88. Sept gas at the Gulf was up slightly to the high-$1.80s. October Midcon gas was talked in the low-to-mid $1.70s, up a couple of cents on the day and almost 10 cents over Sept indices. New York city gate gas was pegged a few cents higher in the $2.07-2.10 area.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 2.7 cents to $2.073. NYMEX said 23,516 contracts traded, down sharply from Tuesday's revised tally of 80,110.
NYMEX October Permian natgas settled 4.5 cents higher at $1.67, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 58 Permian lots traded, down from Tuesday's total of 93.
NYMEX October Permian natgas expires Thursday, Sept 26.

On the KCBT, October expired 6.1 cents higher at $1.707, while deferreds ended up by one-half to four cents. The November East/West spread widened by 0.6 cent to 25.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 656 contracts traded, up from Tuesday's 844.
